newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco says eyeing buys, debt down.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco says eyeing buys, debt down.

text.p: Swedish engineering company Atlas Copco AB head Michael Treschow said on Thursday the group had brought down its debt quickly since the purchase of Milwaukee Electric Tool and was eyeing acquisitions.
"Our cash flow and the balance sheet we have make us braver now than we were at the time of the Milwaukee acquistion," Treschow told a news conference.
"We have gotten the debt down quickly since the purchase and therefore dare to make bigger acquisitions now," he said.
Atlas Copco said in June 1995 it would buy Wisconsin-based Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation for $550 million.
Atlas Copco posted an eight percent rise in 1996 profit after financial items to 3.07 billion crowns compared to market expectations of 3.03 billion crowns.
